investigation.title: Remote Agent Eval Failure: Kubernetes Kata PeerPods VM Resource Exhaustion Blocking Pod Scheduling
investigation.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api because the Kubernetes scheduler could not place the agent pod: only 2 nodes carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource and both are fully allocated, while the remaining 4 nodes do not match the pod's node affinity or selector. The pod remained unscheduled for ~134–143 seconds across all three checks, and no evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) was ever collected, confirming the VM was never provisioned.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agents feature has exhausted the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource on the 2 eligible nodes. The scheduler message "0/6 nodes are available: 2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, 4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector" and "No preemption victims found" indicates that all kata.peerpods.io/vm slots on those 2 nodes are consumed by existing workloads, and preemption cannot free any. Because the pod never schedules, the agent VM is never created, and the eval runner never receives orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, or remoteState — causing a complete contract gap. This is an eval-detected infrastructure capacity constraint, not a confirmed user-traffic outage (no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the evidence).

possibleCauses: PRIMARY — kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource slots are fully consumed on both eligible nodes: existing remote agent VMs or other peer-pod workloads are occupying all available slots, leaving none for new probe pods. This is directly stated in the scheduler message (evidence: failed-check.message, sibling.remote-agent-state, sibling.remote-agent-runtime).

SECONDARY — The cluster has only 2 nodes that satisfy the pod's node affinity/selector for kata peer-pods, and those nodes have a low or fixed capacity ceiling for the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource (e.g., the peer-pod provider quota or node-level resource limit is set too low for concurrent eval probes plus production workloads).

TERTIARY — A prior eval run or production workload leaked remote agent VMs that were not cleaned up, consuming kata.peerpods.io/vm slots that should have been released. The runner uses withCleanup (infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs:1883), but if a prior run crashed before cleanup, leaked VMs could hold slots.

LOWER CONFIDENCE — Node affinity/selector misconfiguration: the 4 non-kata nodes may have had their labels changed or the pod's affinity rules may have become overly restrictive, reducing the schedulable node pool to only 2 nodes and amplifying the capacity problem.

investigation.summary: All three remote-agents checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api at 2026-07-13T20:42–20:47Z with identical Kubernetes scheduler messages reporting that 0/6 nodes could accept a new pod: 2 nodes had insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity and 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the production-api remote-agent swarm had exhausted its allocatable kata.peerpods.io/vm resource slots on the 2 nodes that carry that resource class. The remaining 4 nodes did not satisfy the pod's node affinity/selector, and preemption was not possible on any node. As a result, every eval attempt to create a remote agent pod was stuck Unschedulable for ~134–143 seconds before the probe gave up, producing no evidence and failing all three remote-agent checks. This is an infrastructure-layer scheduling failure localized to the remote-agent VM node pool; it is an eval-detected signal, and no user-traffic or incident data is present in the supplied evidence to confirm a broader production outage.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Eval Failure: Kubernetes Kata PeerPods VM Resource Exhaustion Blocking Pod Scheduling
investigations.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api because the Kubernetes scheduler could not place the agent pod: only 2 nodes carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource and both are fully allocated, while the remaining 4 nodes do not match the pod's node affinity or selector. The pod remained unscheduled for ~134–143 seconds across all three checks, and no evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) was ever collected, confirming the VM was never provisioned.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agents feature has exhausted the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource on the 2 eligible nodes. The scheduler message "0/6 nodes are available: 2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, 4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector" and "No preemption victims found" indicates that all kata.peerpods.io/vm slots on those 2 nodes are consumed by existing workloads, and preemption cannot free any. Because the pod never schedules, the agent VM is never created, and the eval runner never receives orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, or remoteState — causing a complete contract gap. This is an eval-detected infrastructure capacity constraint, not a confirmed user-traffic outage (no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the evidence).

SECONDARY — The cluster has only 2 nodes that satisfy the pod's node affinity/selector for kata peer-pods, and those nodes have a low or fixed capacity ceiling for the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource (e.g., the peer-pod provider quota or node-level resource limit is set too low for concurrent eval probes plus production workloads).

investigations.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Cluster Nodes
investigations.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api because every pod submitted to the Kubernetes cluster was rejected as Unschedulable: the 2 nodes carrying the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource reported insufficient capacity, and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity or selector. Because no agent pod could be scheduled, the eval runner never reached the point of creating an agent or collecting any evidence, leaving all required contract fields (orgId, agentId, model, provider, message) empty.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agents feature has exhausted its kata.peerpods.io/vm resource on the 2 nodes that carry it, and the other 4 nodes are excluded by the pod's node affinity/selector. With 0/6 nodes available and preemption unable to free capacity, every remote-agent pod creation attempt times out unscheduled (~134–145 s), preventing the eval from reaching any application logic and producing zero evidence output. This is a cluster-level infrastructure capacity constraint, not an application code defect. No user-traffic or incident signals are present in the evidence; the impact is scoped to this observability eval.

possibleCauses: PRIMARY — kata.peerpods.io/vm resource exhaustion on the 2 eligible nodes: all available peer-pod VM slots are consumed by existing workloads, leaving no capacity for new eval pods. Supported directly by failed-check.message, sibling.remote-agent-create, and sibling.remote-agent-state.

SECONDARY — node affinity/selector misconfiguration or drift: the pod spec targets only nodes with the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource label, and 4 of 6 nodes do not carry that label or do not match the selector, reducing the schedulable pool to 2 nodes. If those 2 nodes are also at capacity, scheduling fails completely. Supported by the '4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector' clause in failed-check.message.

TERTIARY — cluster under-provisioned for concurrent eval load: if multiple eval runs or production workloads compete for the same 2 kata.peerpods.io/vm nodes simultaneously, transient exhaustion would produce exactly this failure pattern. No concurrent-load evidence is present in the packet, so this remains a hypothesis.

UNLIKELY — eval runner token or org configuration issue: the runner checks for args.token at line 1915 of run-status-probes.mjs and would return SKIP (not fail) if the token were absent. The status is fail with a scheduler message, ruling this out as the primary cause.
